terms.comment: Classically the mission and the envoys sent on it, not a building: Rome sent and received embassies but kept none abroad. Morgan–Owens gives the word for the building too, beside the fuller phrases below.

terms.grammar: noun phrase: sēdēs with the genitive lēgātiōnis
noun phrase: domus with the genitive lēgātī

phrases.latin: Tiberiō prīncipī nūntiāvit Olisīpōnēnsium lēgātiō ob id missa, vīsum audītumque in quōdam specū conchā canentem Trītōnem quā nōscitur fōrmā
phrases.english: an embassy from Lisbon, sent for the purpose, told the emperor Tiberius that a Triton had been seen and heard in a sea cave, blowing his conch, in the shape he is known by

sources: Lewis & Short: legatio · Lewis & Short: sedes · Lewis & Short: legatus · Lewis & Short: domus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. embassy (place, building).
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 4, s.v. ambasciatore.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-plinius), checked against the editions named there.
